presentation.short_description: The Internet Protocol version 4 addressing and packet-delivery protocol used by the diagnosed network path.

entities.purpose: Represent IPv4 addressing and packet delivery independently from address-assignment protocols such as DHCP.
entities.education_text: A host can have working IPv6 while its IPv4 configuration or DHCPv4 lease path is unavailable.

presentation.short_description: The Internet Protocol version 6 addressing and packet-delivery protocol.

entities.purpose: Represent IPv6 state separately when comparing protocol-specific reachability and address assignment.
entities.education_text: Healthy IPv6 connectivity does not prove that IPv4 addressing or DHCPv4 is healthy.

presentation.short_description: The DHCP server has no reusable address available for a requesting client.

entities.education_text: Pool exhaustion is a server-side actionable cause of a client-visible lease failure; stale reservations are one possible source of occupied capacity.

presentation.short_description: Requests or releases an Internet Protocol version 4 (IPv4) lease from a Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) service and can show the client exchange.

illustration.alt_text: Dark service console with abstract dhclient Lease Request output beside enterprise server hardware.
illustration.caption: Canonical command illustration for dhclient Lease Request.
illustration.license_note: Generated for TASK-011 with OpenAI built-in image generation; repository use follows applicable OpenAI terms and the repository license.

entities.purpose: Release and request an IPv4 DHCP lease while recording Discover, Offer, Request, and acknowledgement behavior.
entities.education_text: Command syntax and direct-server options vary by client version; preserve the exact command and output in the work record.

presentation.short_description: Safely removes all external power, discharges residual state, and then compares symptoms after controlled re-energization.

illustration.alt_text: Night-shift server test setup for Residual-Power Drain Test, staged without indicating a result.
illustration.caption: Canonical test illustration for Residual-Power Drain Test.
illustration.license_note: Generated for TASK-011 with OpenAI built-in image generation; repository use follows applicable OpenAI terms and the repository license.

evidence_rules.notes: Symptom changes after a complete discharge can narrow power-state hypotheses but do not by themselves prove a PSU repair.
Persistent or changed power behavior becomes Evidence after the controlled reset.
A partial recovery can leave a board or another subsystem hypothesis unresolved.

entities.education_text: Follow the approved de-energization procedure and platform instructions; remove every redundant power feed before discharge.

presentation.short_description: Measures documented power rails and power-good signals with an appropriate meter and the platform connector pinout.

illustration.alt_text: Night-shift server test setup for Power Output Voltage Measurement, staged without indicating a result.
illustration.caption: Canonical test illustration for Power Output Voltage Measurement.
illustration.license_note: Generated for TASK-011 with OpenAI built-in image generation; repository use follows applicable OpenAI terms and the repository license.

evidence_rules.notes: Interpret measurements only against the approved connector, load, tolerance, and power-state specification.
Comparing source and distributed rails can isolate a supply from the downstream distribution path.

entities.education_text: Do not generalize an Advanced Technology Extended (ATX) pinout to a proprietary or hot-swap server interface; use model-specific documentation and electrical-safety controls.

presentation.short_description: Interprets a Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) client exchange to distinguish an absent server offer from client-side address-configuration problems.

illustration.alt_text: Night-shift server test setup for DHCP Transaction Trace, staged without indicating a result.
illustration.caption: Canonical test illustration for DHCP Transaction Trace.
illustration.license_note: Generated for TASK-011 with OpenAI built-in image generation; repository use follows applicable OpenAI terms and the repository license.

evidence_rules.notes: Discover without Offer supports a DHCP service or capacity path; a completed lease can rule out the current lease-failure state.
An absent Offer is compatible with pool exhaustion but does not confirm the server-side cause without a pool audit.

entities.education_text: Preserve the exact Discover, Offer, Request, acknowledgement, timeout, and server-identity observations.

presentation.short_description: Inspects free-address capacity, active leases, exclusions, and stale reservations on the Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) service.

illustration.alt_text: Night-shift server test setup for DHCP Address Pool Audit, staged without indicating a result.
illustration.caption: Canonical test illustration for DHCP Address Pool Audit.
illustration.license_note: Generated for TASK-011 with OpenAI built-in image generation; repository use follows applicable OpenAI terms and the repository license.

evidence_rules.notes: Zero available addresses with occupied or stale allocations can confirm the actionable capacity fault.
The audit explains one server-side path to the client-visible lease failure.

entities.education_text: Record scope utilization and the specific allocation state; do not delete active reservations merely because the pool is full.

presentation.short_description: Reads processor and platform temperature telemetry through an operating-system sensor utility.

capabilities: Record temperature change during a controlled workload
Provide telemetry when a BMC console is unavailable
safety_notes: Confirm that the utility reports the intended sensor and units before interpreting thresholds.
Stop the workload if the platform reaches its approved thermal limit or becomes unstable.

presentation.short_description: Removes verified stale reservations or allocations to restore reusable DHCP address capacity.

steps_summary: Confirm address-pool exhaustion and identify allocations that are genuinely stale.
Preserve required reservations and remove only the stale entries authorized for cleanup.
Confirm that reusable capacity is available before requesting a new client lease.
entities.education_text: The repair changes DHCP server state; it is distinct from correcting one client's static address.

presentation.short_description: Preserves recoverable data, rebuilds the affected system or storage configuration, and restores the verified backup when in-place reconstruction cannot complete.

steps_summary: Capture a full recoverable backup and verify that it can be read before destructive reconstruction.
Record array members, bay mapping, configuration, and the isolated failure path.
Rebuild the approved system and storage configuration without inventing an unverified component replacement.
Restore the backup and perform the required boot, storage, and service validations.
entities.education_text: This is a recovery path when in-place array reconstruction cannot safely complete; it is not the same procedure as a normal RAID parity rebuild.

presentation.short_description: Confirms that the repaired client receives the expected lease and usable network configuration from the intended DHCP service.

success_conditions: The client obtains a new IPv4 lease from the expected DHCP service.
The assigned address, prefix, gateway, lease lifetime, and required options match the authored network expectations.
The repaired path passes the Ticket's required connectivity check.
entities.education_text: A successful ping alone does not prove that the expected DHCP server supplied the correct lease and options.

presentation.display_name: Exhausted DHCP Pool Causes Lease Failure
presentation.short_description: An address pool with no reusable capacity prevents a requesting client from obtaining a lease.

conditions: The client requests an address from the exhausted pool.
No reusable allocation is available under the active DHCP policy.
entities.notes: Pool exhaustion is one actionable cause of lease failure, not a claim that every absent lease has this cause.
